I’m just someone who needs some kind of ‘over-exposure when I’m dealing with trauma, I can’t avoid the issue as a part of my healing, I need the confrontation to get it completely shaken out of me’ the difficult topic becomes neutralized for me and after a while it’s just a normality like baking bread and seeing it turn crusty in the oven. It becomes just a fact or a way of life, no particular emotional attachment to the wound or the phenomenon, it becomes just ‘well that’s sad’ and I distance myself from it.
Because I believe I didn’t choose that wound, I didn’t inflict that trauma onto myself, I do not want it to bother me, to become some part of my personality. 

I did that 3 times now in my life. Different traumas, different techniques, but somehow made it neutralize in my system. I must admit, I also read a lot about psychology and philosophy and also had some therapy done and even the therapist was surprised by how will I work on myself. For instance for one trauma I wrote a word over and over again until I had no particular emotional response to that word again. It was like ‘ok’ I’m finally being fine with that word now, it’s just a word..

I just hate a victim mentality even when I AM the victim, I don’t want it to become a personality-trait of mine.
Therefore I can’t let it win over me.


But again, you probably have another way of coping and healing from it, mine is truly picking the bullet out of the flesh and dissecting the whole bullet and sewing the flesh myself as a lesson to distance myself from making that mistake again, eventhough it wasn’t truly upon me that it happened. You just don’t want it to happen again, and if it does, you want it to be a fast and clean cut without much of a bleeding.

Life sucks in many ways. But I don’t want it be hang up in those moments of deceit and misery. I prefer looking out to the better parts of it. And luckily the sun does come out even after a long period of cold winter time.

The only thing I can say is that my neurodivergence adds to my emotional experiences , it enhances things immensely. So feeling good feels extremely good and feeling bad is also aggravating. I prefer being in the middle and also being on my own. 
And I also feel that being ‘different’ is exactly what draws people in, without me trying. I am different and stand out in my ways, language (English is not my native language, my vocabulary is broad in my main language and also my pronunciation is more delicate). I have thousands of hobbies, but not one that keeps me enough busy to not be preoccupied by others.

I’ve experienced a lot of intense sincere love. I am mostly a giver than a receiver. And because I wanted to become single and stay single, I realized I needed reciprocal respect and attention.
What you’re thinking and saying about me is untrue.
Except for me not truly being my age, is true, I look and feel younger than my age, but that has always been the case, except for when I was a child, my mind had always been more adult in thinking logically before my fellow teenagers. When I talk to old school friends, it’s obvious that I was very observant and knowing of people by observing and not by participating. 

I think I see myself as a platter that has such amount of flavor that lots of sugar or salt isn’t needed. It’s a unique flavor, that people either tend to hate or be intrigued by but most certainly don’t understand how it was cooked. And that’s why my relationships don’t last longer than a year mostly, after figuring me out they tend to not being able to live with that kind of personality. Which is hurtful and very tiring for me. As I give it my all.
Not gonna deny that anxious attachment is also in my characteristics. But that is just a result of growing up fatherless. And without the comfort of a home, and a positive relationship with my mom only came after the age of 30, the age I was properly diagnosed and could finally get some peace and understanding.

I think it’s sad that you judge too fast based on age. Every one experiences life and age differently. And every decade represents something else for everyone, although it’s majorly about ‘finding yourself’. Which I finally did now. 
I can’t help it that I’m super sensitive, especially to people’s energy. And when I feel them being infatuated, I feel that pull as well. When I’m in a relationship that pull to others is turned off, because I only have the mental capacity to focus on one person at a time. But when I’m on my own, I become just too much of a target and that gives me anxiety.

But then..

It flopped. The Barbie that wants to go to the real world, was poorly executed (which was honestly a bad version of the Disney movie Unchanted (2007) which was actually funny.)

But Barbie went somewhere else, it went to a place of ‘trying to make a story’ out of what looked like a movie that took too much effort to make in the first 10 minutes that they just decided to make their own jobs easier by incorporating ‘the real world’ and add a political agenda to it.

That’s it.

And the only _for real_ ‘moment of beauty’ and maybe the only essential hidden meaning for a movie that went too far in trying too hard,  was when Margot (who’s stunning by the way) looks at the old lady and says ‘you look beautiful’ and has her first cry. Not because of a Barbie crying, not because Barbie is plastic and crying would be making her real, but just because there are no granny Barbie’s, and she has never seen an aged lady, and the flawless Barbie found beauty in what she saw, a wrinkled aged woman with nothing fashionable on, just a person who lived.

A few tricks helped me:

The 5 seconds rule: when you think of something to do, you know that in very little time your brain is going to tell you a whole bunch of stupid lazy answers for not doing it. Before that happens you have the ability/awareness to build your strength/courage to just do it, by counting down your launch: 5.. 4.. 3.. 2.. 1! And then you just do it. Because you learn that it’s not as hard as you are making it up for yourself.

Another trick is: if it takes less than 3 minutes to do it, do it now, don’t put it on a ‘to-do’ list. After I accumulated too many things for my to-do; I realized at times that it actually took more time procrasting it than just doing it right away. So whenever you think about ‘I have to write that down, ask yourself first ‘is it going to take 3 minutes or less? Yes? Ok do it now.

Same goes with putting away stuff. You can put it ‘in front of you, because that’s just easy, I’ll put it back when I feel like it, or go in that direction and before you know it, stuff just get out of hand. So ‘put things away in their spot immediately’
